newsitem.title: CHINA: Washington mayor in Beijing duck diplomacy.
newsitem.headline: Washington mayor in Beijing duck diplomacy.

text.p: Washington, D.C., Mayor Marion Barry on Tuesday crowned a six-day visit to boost economic exchanges with Beijing by signing a memorandum aimed at bringing the Chinese capital's famous roast duck to the United States.

Barry signed the memorandum with Beijing's acting mayor Jia Qinglin after talks with a Beijing-based restaurant chain, one of two potential commercial deals touted by the Washington mayor as the fruits of his visit.
"We've had some very fruitful relations with the Peking (Beijing) duck people," Barry told reporters.

Barry said he was excited at the idea of opening a Washington branch of the Quanjude Roast Duck Group, one of a number of Beijing restaurants that serve the classic crispy-skinned, wood-smoked duck dish.
Officials from both sides would soon start to hammer out the details of the duck deal, he said without elaborating.
Barry said his delegation had also held talks with Friendship Commercial Group on opening a shop in Washington to sell Chinese goods and handicrafts.
"Those (deals) are some budding flowers, budding fruits that we hope to work hard on," he said.
The Washington delegation had lobbied their Chinese hosts to ease restrictions on travelling abroad, he said.
"We have to work hard to try to get them to allow more people to come to Washington," he said.
Beijing officials on Monday praised Barry for boosting sisterly ties between the two capitals and said they wanted to learn from the U.S. city's urban development.
Washington is virtually bankrupt. The financial management of the District of Columbia was taken over in February 1995 by a federal control board.
Jia assumed his Beijing post last month in a long-delayed reshuffle following a 1995 corruption scandal involving a vice-mayor, who later committed suicide.
Barry, a liberal Democrat and civil rights leader, is himself no stranger to controversy, having served a jail term in 1990 on a federal drugs charge.
